assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, active GLP-1(7-36) amide, insulinotropic and satiety actions) led to therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. This is a clear, specific discovery chain with very large and visible clinical impact and a discernible change in the field.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology of the active incretin peptide, Drucker the receptor biology, gut-derived actions and translational link, and Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the active peptide form. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen drove industrial development of long-acting analogues but is the most natural fourth name; the three-person cap forces a choice, and Mojsov credit is debated.
assessment.maturity: Therapeutic confirmation is extensive and independent across multiple drug classes and large outcome trials; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority dispute around Mojsov's contribution versus others in the early peptide work.
Whether the prize should reward basic physiology, the drug-development step (Knudsen), or both is unresolved.
I am relying on recalled literature and have not independently verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, establishing a new therapeutic modality in cancer. The concept is original and the clinical consequence is large.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June drove the design and clinical validation of costimulated CAR constructs for CD19 therapy; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials. The configuration is plausible, but Zelig Eshhar and others who originated the chimeric receptor concept are not among the supplied names, which limits fairness of this credit set.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent clinical confirmation over a decade; durability is established in hematologic cancers, whereas solid-tumor efficacy remains limited.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric-receptor concept lies outside the supplied names.
Late toxicities and secondary malignancies are still being characterized.
Some recalled details may be imprecise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provides cell-type-specific control of neural activity with light and has become a foundational method across neuroscience, grounded in the discovery and characterization of channelrhodopsins. It is original, widely adopted and enabling for circuit dissection.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are the identification and electrophysiological characterization of channelrhodopsin (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and the demonstration of its use for millisecond neuronal control (Boyden, Deisseroth). With six credited names and a three-laureate cap, an arbitrary subset leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, so the allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Technique is firmly validated and used worldwide; clinical translation is early (retinal restoration), but a methods prize rests on the discovery and its impact on research rather than therapy.
uncertainties: Allocation among at least six credited people is difficult and contested.
Nobel tradition regarding method versus discovery adds uncertainty.
Clinical impact is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of BCL11A as a repressor of fetal hemoglobin switching, and its therapeutic reactivation, leads to a mechanism-based treatment of sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. It links human genetic variation to regulation and then to an approved gene-editing therapy.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran established BCL11A's role in hemoglobin switching, with human genetic association work in this area; Bauer led the enhancer-editing therapeutic strategy. Swee Lay Thein contributed human genetic mapping of fetal hemoglobin modifiers, so the choice excludes one credited contributor.
assessment.maturity: An approved therapy and independent clinical confirmation exist, but follow-up remains relatively short and the work is recent, so timing may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Credit among genetic-association and mechanistic contributions is unresolved.
Long-term durability and access limits of the therapy are not yet established.
Recalled facts not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of BCR-ABL kinase activity with imatinib transformed chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease to a manageable one and validated oncogene-directed therapy broadly. The discovery is clear and its impact lasting.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the chemistry-to-kinase-inhibitor program, Druker the clinical translation, and Sawyers resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. The configuration is defensible, though Nowell, Rowley, and the discoverers of BCR-ABL are not within the supplied names, and the earlier Philadelphia chromosome and ABL work are part of a larger chain.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of independent follow-up. Recognition is not premature; the question is whether it is still a priority relative to others.
uncertainties: The prior chain of discoveries (Philadelphia chromosome, fusion gene) may be seen as the more fundamental credit.
Industrial versus academic credit allocation is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR and the mTOR pathway as a central regulator of cell growth, nutrient sensing and metabolism has broad consequences for cancer, metabolism, aging and immunosuppression. The concept is original and has reshaped cell physiology.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR as the target of rapamycin in yeast and defined its function, which is the decisive step. Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR partners and nutrient-sensing mechanisms; Schreiber contributed rapamycin and FKBP12 chemical biology. Sabatini's inclusion is a judgement; the central claim rests with Hall.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed across systems; clinical consequences (rapalogs) are real but more modest than the basic biology. Recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Sabatini's standing is complicated by non-scientific events, which is not a scientific matter but could affect committee deliberation.
Allocation between yeast genetics and mammalian pathway work is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identification and its loss in narcolepsy type 1 established a molecular basis for a sleep disorder and led to orexin receptor antagonists for insomnia. It is original, mechanistically clear and clinically meaningful.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa discovered orexin and its receptors and linked them to feeding and wakefulness; Mignot identified the canine narcolepsy gene (Hcrtr2) and human orexin deficiency, while de Lecea and Kilduff independently identified hypocretins. Priority between independent discoveries is a recognized allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by independent groups, with drugs in clinical use, but the interpretation of orexin-deficiency mechanisms (possibly autoimmune) is still evolving.
uncertainties: Parallel independent discovery of hypocretin versus orexin complicates credit.
Cause of orexin neuron loss in narcolepsy remains incompletely resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune signaling, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and senescence. It is a new, coherent signaling axis with growing relevance.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber and Ishikawa identified STING; credit for later structural and mechanistic work lies among additional names. A three-person set of Chen, Barber and Ishikawa is plausible but Ishikawa's role may be seen as smaller than that of others in the field.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in basic science, though therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) is not yet validated clinically, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is not established.
Distribution of credit for STING versus cGAS and mechanistic follow-up is debated.
